blocks.text: I can interpret graphs that model real-life situations graphically.
Tap the key word to see what it means.

items.def: The rate of change is how one variable changes with respect to another. If the change is constant, there is a linear relationship between the variables.

blocks.text: If distance increases at a constant rate over time, that means a {constant speed}.
Distance-time graphs are a type of graph which model the distance an object travels with respect to time.

items: Because we are modelling the distance moved as time progresses, we plot **time on the x-axis**.
Always look at the units: time might be seconds, minutes or hours, and distance might be metres or kilometres.

blocks.text: A model might not be perfect, but it gives us a general idea of what is happening in a real-life situation.

slides.title: Reading a point on the graph

blocks.text: Aisha recorded a jog. She modelled it as a straight line that starts at the origin (0, 0) and passes through the point (10, 2000). Time is in minutes and distance is in metres.

blocks.label: What does the point (10, 2000) mean?
blocks.text: She ran a total of 2000 metres (2 km) in 10 minutes.

blocks.label: How far after 5 minutes?
blocks.text: After 5 minutes she had run 1000 metres (1 km). In double the time (10 minutes) she went double the distance (2000 metres).
On a distance-time graph, a diagonal line represents moving at a constant speed. The steeper the line, the faster the movement.

Aisha’s longer route: after 8 minutes she had run 1600 metres, then the graph had a line segment that was less steep (a smaller gradient). She started to run at a slower speed, but it was still a straight line, so still a consistent speed.

blocks.label: What does a horizontal line mean?
blocks.text: There is no increase in distance in that time. If time passes 6 minutes along the x-axis and the line is flat, she was stationary for 6 minutes.
Read each story and choose the pattern of line segments that fits it. Assume each moving part is at a constant speed.

blocks.q: A cyclist rides quickly, stops for a rest, then rides on more slowly. Which pattern of lines fits?
options: Steep line, horizontal line, less steep line
Steep line, less steep line, horizontal line
Steep line, horizontal line, steeper line
blocks.why: Fast means a steep line, stopping means a horizontal line, and slower means a less steep line.

blocks.q: A walker sets off slowly, walks faster, then stops. Which pattern of lines fits?
options: Steep line, less steep line, horizontal line
Less steep line, steeper line, horizontal line
Horizontal line, less steep line, steep line
blocks.why: Slow first is a less steep line, faster next is a steeper line, and stopping at the end is a horizontal line.

blocks.text: When you interpret a graph, it is important to understand what is meant by distance. Check the label on the y-axis.

items.title: Distance from home
items.sub: distance from a fixed start point

blocks.text: If we are measuring total distance travelled, the line segments will always have a positive (or zero) gradient, because distance travelled cannot decrease as time increases.
If we are measuring distance from a fixed start point (home), then a line segment with a **negative gradient** represents the **return journey**.

blocks.q: Which type of graph does each statement describe?

items.text: The line can slope downwards to show the return journey
The y-axis shows how far you are from a fixed start point
The distance can only stay the same or increase

blocks.text: Time is always moving forwards. That rules out two kinds of line on distance-time graphs.
Distance-time graphs cannot have vertical lines, and they cannot have lines going backwards in time. This is also true for a distance from home graph.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Going down in a lift does not make a total-distance line slope downwards. The y-axis is total distance, so the distance travelled always increases, no matter which direction you are travelling in.

blocks.q: On a distance from home graph, is each line segment possible or impossible?

items.text: A line with a negative gradient that moves forwards in time
A line that goes backwards in time

blocks.q: On a graph of TOTAL distance travelled, is a line segment with a negative gradient possible?
options: Yes, it shows the return journey
blocks.why: Total distance travelled cannot decrease, so its line segments have a positive or zero gradient.

blocks.text: A car’s distance-time graph shows the journey took 6 hours 30 minutes. The car stopped for 30 minutes at two separate points. The car’s journey clock said 5 hours 30 minutes.

items: Time missing: 6 h 30 min − 5 h 30 min = 1 hour.
So the journey clock may have been turned off while the car was stationary.

blocks.text: To find the overall distance, look at the furthest distance reached at the end of the graph. To find when the speed was highest, look for the **steepest** line segment.

slides.title: Other real-life graphs: filling a bath

blocks.text: We can use graphs to model all sorts of scenarios. In a depth-time graph, time is on the x-axis and the depth of water is on the y-axis. Water runs into the bath at a constant rate.

items: A bath modelled as a cuboid has the same cross section at all depths, so the depth changes at a constant rate. That gives a **linear graph**.
A shorter bath of the same width fills quicker. It is still linear, but steeper.
A bath with a ledge for a seat: the depth rises at a constant rate until the water reaches the ledge, then still at a constant rate but slower (less steep).
A bath with angled ends keeps getting wider, so the rate the depth increases is continually slowing. At no point is it a constant rate.

blocks.q: Water is poured at a constant rate into a container with vertical sides. What is the depth-time graph like?
blocks.why: The cross section is the same at all depths, so the depth changes at a constant rate, which gives a linear graph.

blocks.q: In a bath with a ledge for a seat, what happens to the rate the depth increases once the water passes the ledge?
options: It slows down but is still constant
blocks.why: The seat adds extra space, so the depth still rises at a constant rate but slower, giving a less steep line segment.

blocks.q: Why is a vertical line impossible on a depth-time graph?
options: Time always has to be increasing
blocks.why: Like distance-time graphs, time is on the x-axis and time always has to be increasing.

blocks.text: Here is what each type of line could show on a depth-time graph.

items.title: Line sloping up
items.sub: depth increasing at a constant rate, like a container with vertical sides being filled at a constant rate

items.title: Horizontal line
items.sub: depth constant, maybe the water is turned off for a length of time

items.title: Line sloping down
items.sub: depth decreasing at a constant rate, maybe water being drained

items: Distance-time graphs can tell us about a journey. Time is plotted on the x-axis and distance on the y-axis.
Diagonal lines represent constant speed, and horizontal lines represent no movement.
If the y-axis represents distance from a fixed point, a downwards sloping line represents the journey back towards the start point.
Vertical lines and lines going backwards in time are impossible.
If the rate of change is constant, the graph will be linear.

flashcards.front: What is the rate of change?
flashcards.back: How one variable changes with respect to another. If the change is constant, there is a linear relationship between the variables.

flashcards.front: What is plotted on the x-axis of a distance-time graph?
What does a diagonal line mean on a distance-time graph?
On a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line mean?
What does a horizontal line mean on a distance-time graph?
flashcards.back: No movement: time passes but the distance does not increase (the object is stationary).

flashcards.front: Why can a total distance-time graph never slope downwards?
flashcards.back: Total distance travelled cannot decrease as time increases, so gradients are positive or zero.

flashcards.front: On a distance from home graph, what does a negative gradient show?
flashcards.back: The return journey (getting closer to the start point as time progresses).

flashcards.front: Why is a vertical line impossible on a distance-time graph?
flashcards.back: It would mean travelling a distance in zero time. Time has to move forward.

flashcards.front: Why are lines going backwards in time impossible?
flashcards.back: The horizontal axis is time, and time always has to move forward (increase).

flashcards.front: How do you find the overall distance of a journey on a distance-time graph?
flashcards.back: Read the y-coordinate at the end of the final line segment.

flashcards.front: How do you spot the fastest part of a distance-time graph?
flashcards.back: Look for the steepest line segment.

flashcards.front: Water is poured at a constant rate into a container with vertical sides. What is the depth-time graph like?
flashcards.back: A straight (linear) line, because the depth changes at a constant rate.

flashcards.front: In a bath with angled ends, how does the depth increase as it fills?
flashcards.back: The rate the depth increases is continually slowing, because the bath keeps getting wider.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Checking and securing understanding of reading from context-based graphs
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question in a few words or a number. Include units where the question asks for them.

questions.prompt: On a distance-time graph, which axis is time plotted on? Answer x or y.
questions.explanation: We plot time on the x-axis because we are modelling the distance moved as time progresses.

questions.prompt: A straight line on a distance-time graph starts at (0, 0) and passes through (10, 2000). Time is in minutes and distance in metres. How many metres had been travelled after 5 minutes?
questions.explanation: In half the time (5 minutes) the constant-speed line has covered half of 2000 m, which is 1000 m.

questions.prompt: On Aisha’s graph, a horizontal line segment runs from 14 minutes to 20 minutes. For how many minutes was she stationary?
questions.explanation: Between 14 and 20 minutes time passes but the distance does not increase: 20 − 14 = 6 minutes.

questions.prompt: A car journey takes 6 hours 30 minutes. The car stops twice for 30 minutes each time. The journey clock is turned off whenever the car is stationary. What time does the journey clock show?
questions.explanation: The two stops add up to 1 hour, and 6 h 30 min − 1 h = 5 h 30 min.

questions.prompt: A car’s distance-time graph ends at the point (5.5, 310), where time is in hours and distance is in kilometres. How many kilometres was the overall journey?
questions.explanation: On a distance-time graph the overall distance is the y-coordinate of the end of the final line segment.

questions.prompt: On a graph of TOTAL distance travelled, can a line segment ever slope downwards? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: Total distance travelled cannot decrease as time increases.

questions.prompt: On a distance from home graph, a line segment slopes downwards as time moves forwards. Is the object moving towards or away from home?
questions.explanation: A negative gradient on a distance from home graph represents the return journey, getting closer to home.

questions.prompt: A vertical line on a distance-time graph would mean distance travelled in how much time?
questions.explanation: A vertical line is a change in distance without a change in time, which is impossible.

questions.prompt: Water runs at a constant rate into a bath with vertical sides (a cuboid). Is the depth-time graph linear or curved?
questions.explanation: The cross section is the same at all depths, so the depth changes at a constant rate, giving a linear graph.

questions.prompt: A bath has a ledge for a seat. Once the water reaches the ledge, does the depth rise faster or slower than before?
questions.explanation: The seat adds extra space, so the depth still increases at a constant rate but more slowly, a less steep line segment.
